content.heading: Fundamental Rights — Part III scheme
content.text: Part III of the Constitution of India (Articles 12 to 35) confers Fundamental Rights. Article 12 defines the State. Article 13 addresses laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights. Substantive rights span equality (Articles 14 to 18), freedoms (Article 19), protection in respect of conviction (Article 20), life and personal liberty (Article 21), education (Article 21A), protection against arrest and detention in certain cases (Article 22), protection against exploitation (Articles 23 and 24), freedom of religion (Articles 25 to 28), cultural and educational rights (Articles 29 and 30), and constitutional remedies (Article 32). Article 31 as a Fundamental Right to property stands omitted; Articles 31A to 31C and Article 300A address property-related savings and the current property clause. Articles 33 to 35 address Armed Forces modifications, martial law, and legislation for Part III. Canonical article texts live under provision:india:constitution-art-*.
